questions.question: What are Virtual Threads in Java?
questions.answer:
Virtual Threads are lightweight threads introduced as a preview feature in Java 19 and finalized in Java 21.

They are managed by JVM instead of directly mapping one-to-one to operating system threads.

They help applications handle thousands or millions of concurrent I/O-bound tasks with less thread-management overhead.

Platform Thread vs Virtual Thread

| Platform Thread | Virtual Thread |
| --- | --- |
| OS thread based | JVM managed |
| Higher resource overhead | Lower resource overhead |
| Limited concurrency | High concurrency |
| Suitable for CPU and I/O tasks | Particularly useful for I/O-bound tasks |
| Created using new Thread() | Created using virtual thread APIs |

Where do we use Virtual Threads?

- Calling multiple REST APIs.
- Database operations.
- External service integrations.
- I/O-intensive microservices.
Important: Virtual Threads improve concurrency, not CPU processing speed.

questions.question: Method Overloading - Output Prediction
questions.answer:
What happens when you execute the following Java program?

Complete Java Program:

Compilation Error – Ambiguous Method Call
Why?

Both methods are applicable.

| Method | First argument | Second argument |
| --- | --- | --- |
| add(int, long) | Exact match | int → long |
| add(long, int) | int → long | Exact match |
Both methods have one exact match and one widening conversion.

The compiler cannot decide which method is more specific.

How to resolve it?

- `obj.add(9, 10L)` calls `add(int, long)`: the first argument is an exact match, and `10L` is a `long`.
- `obj.add(9L, 10)` calls `add(long, int)`: `9L` is a `long`, and the second argument is an exact match.

Concept: Method Overloading and Compile-time Polymorphism.

questions.question: What are the New Features Introduced in Spring Boot 3?
questions.answer:
Spring Boot 3 introduced several improvements, including Java 17 baseline support, Spring Framework 6, Jakarta EE migration, Native Image support, AOT processing and improved observability.

Important Features
| Feature | Explanation |
| --- | --- |
| Java 17 baseline | Minimum Java version is 17 |
| Spring Framework 6 | New framework generation |
| Jakarta EE 9+ | Migration from javax to jakarta packages |
| GraalVM Native Image | Build native executable applications |
| AOT Processing | Ahead-of-time processing |
| Observability | Micrometer Observation support |
| Spring Security 6 | Updated security framework |
| HTTP Interfaces | Declarative HTTP clients through Spring Framework |

2. Native Image Support

With GraalVM Native Image, we can compile Java applications into native executables.

Advantages:

- Faster startup.
- Lower memory footprint in suitable applications.

Observability helps monitor applications using:

- Metrics
- Logs

| Older security generation | Spring Security 6 |

questions.question: What is ExecutorService? Have You Used It in Spring Boot?
questions.answer:
ExecutorService is an interface in Java's concurrency framework. It manages the execution of asynchronous tasks using threads and thread pools.

Instead of manually creating threads for every task, we submit tasks to ExecutorService.

Important Methods
| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| execute() | Execute a Runnable task |
| submit() | Submit a task and return Future |
| shutdown() | Stop accepting new tasks |
| shutdownNow() | Attempt to stop running tasks |
| isTerminated() | Check whether all tasks have completed |
| awaitTermination() | Wait for executor termination |

ExecutorService vs Virtual Threads
| ExecutorService with a fixed pool | Virtual-thread-per-task executor |
| --- | --- |
| Uses a limited number of threads | Creates a virtual thread for each task |
| Pool size needs configuration | No fixed pool size is required |
| Tasks may wait when all pool threads are busy | Can handle many concurrent I/O-bound tasks |
| Useful when concurrency should be limited | Useful for many I/O-bound tasks |

Important: Virtual Threads and ExecutorService are not competitors. newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor() itself returns an ExecutorService.
